figures.finding: The only actor-producer agreement found for Indian screen work is the memorandum of understanding signed on 1 May 2014 by CINTAA, the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) and the Indian Film and TV Producers' Council (IFTPC) for Mumbai television: it requires written contracts handed to the actor within 15 days of the shoot starting and sets payment deadlines, but leaves the day fee to negotiation.

sources.said: the memorandum of understanding (MoU) inked between the Cine & TV Artistes Association (CINTAA), the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), and the Indian Film and TV Producers’ Council (IIFTPC) on 1 May.

all engagements of actors will be recorded in writing and it will be mandatory for producers to give a copy of the contract/agreement to such actors before commencement of the shoot or not later than 15 days after commencement of the shoot.

another clause of the MoU, which deals with actors who are engaged up to only five days per month and whose per day remuneration is only up to Rs 5,000, has been the subject of much debate. The clause states that such actors will be paid within five days of their last day of shooting. Morever, the production house will fix their per-day remuneration after negotiations with them, and Rs 300 will be paid in cash over and above the agreed per day remuneration after completion of the day’s shoot. In the event the actor is part of a mythological/historical/weekend show, the payment will be made within 21 days of his/her day of shooting.
He pointed out that the MoU requires only five lead actors, as decided by the producer, to sign the three-year contract with him/her.

figures.finding: No collective agreement or published rate card sets a minimum fee for an actor in Indian film or television: the day fee is negotiated with the production house, most TV and web actors work by the day, and pay follows a 60-to-90-day cycle that CINTAA's president called very unfair in July 2026.

value.hours: no agreed cap; CINTAA and FWICE asked in June 2020 for 8-hour shifts; actors report 12 to 15 hour days on daily soaps

figures.finding: The actors' union for Hindi film and television is CINTAA (Cine & TV Artistes' Association, Mumbai): an applicant files a INR 500 form, then holds a first-year and a second-year work permit at INR 10,000 each, and in the third year, after an assessment of work done, may become a regular member for INR 10,000 plus a INR 500 welfare fund and INR 1,200 a year; foreigners and NRIs can take a work permit for INR 10,000.

value.eligibility: one year of training, or a show reel, or for a fresher a production house's letter for a significant character or an on-camera audition at CINTAA
value.membershipRequired: not stated by any source read; CINTAA bye-laws bar replacing an artist without the artist's or CINTAA's NOC

figures.applies: India, performers in feature films, TV serials, telefilms, live performance, ads and digital media resident in India; fees as published 2026.

sources.said: Membership of CINTAA is meant for any Indian national performer who is physically, mentally and emotionally fit to perform as an artist and who plays or has been engaged to play a significant role in a feature film, TV serials, Tele films, live performances, advertisement films shown on screen, digital or any new media who reside within the boundary of the Union of India.

One can become a CINTAA member by submitting the duly filled Membership Form of Rs. 500/- (non-refundable) along with the required documents. If approved, he/she can obtain 1st year work permit by paying entrance fees of Rs. 10,000/- (validity 1 year).
If admitted for regular membership, he/she will have to pay one time entrance fees of Rs. 10,000, plus membership welfare fund of Rs. 500/-  and a regular subscription of Rs. 1200/- per annum.

Foreign Nationals as well as Non- Resident Indians can obtain a work permit for limited time. This work-permit shall be granted for a year or the period of project/ valid passport and employment visa validity, whichever is less by paying fees of Rs. 10,000/- for limited time.
For Freshers -Letter of employment from a production house/channel for a significant character in a film/TV show or an on-camera audition in CINTAA’s office.
Rs.1,00,000 (one-time, non-refundable)
No Artist shall be replaced without obtaining their/ CINTAA’s NOC.
CINTAA Tower, 5th floor, Next to Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital Gate No - 4, Four Bunglow, Andheri West, Mumbai - 400 053.

figures.finding: CINTAA's constitution asks that at least half of a child artiste's (under 18) payment be set aside in fixed deposits or bonds maturing at 18, that a child miss no more than 10 school days a year for shooting, and that a parent or guardian may stay on set.

sources.said: Provided that a minimum of 50% of the payment must be set aside for children in fixed deposits or bonds that mature when they reach the age of 18 years.
The child should not miss school on account of shooting, for more than 10 days in an academic year work.
Parent/Guardian/Caretaker of the children should be allowed to remain with the children during shooting.

figures.finding: Under the Labour Codes no employer may pay any employee less than the minimum wage the government notifies, now for all employees and not only scheduled trades; audio-visual workers, which now include dubbing artists and stunt persons, must be engaged on a written agreement that states wages and hours, with 8 hours a day and 48 a week and overtime at twice the rate.
